findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no measuring device for temperatures regarding the heat at the dish machine. Facility needs a maximum registering thermometer and/or heat test strips in order to verify that the dish machine is heating to at least 160F. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 2/13/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112  (Pf) Hot water sanitizing rinse at dish machine is less than 180F. Repair unit so that hot water rinse is maintained between 180F to 194F. 

Dish machine on arrival was showing a fluctuating rinse temperature on the display. A maximum registering tape was used to check the temperature and would not register (no collar change). Maintenance was contacted and the booster attached to the machine adjusted to requirements during the inspection.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

Observed a scoop in the flour bin to be laying with the handle touching the flour. Discussed the possible contamination that this allows with hand contact and instructed the PIC to store the scoop with the handle extending out of the food or clean and dry.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed bleach and soap being mixed in the sanitizing solution bucket. Bucket was recreated with only bleach in solution during the inspection. Cease combining soap with bleach. Should you want to use a detergent to clean surfaces, use a specific bucket with only soap first and then use a solution of only 100ppm Cl to wipe down surfaces after the soap. Staff uses soap to cut through grease and sugars.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.
